provider_proposal.incident_summary: Synthetic SEV2 incident where RFQ handling degraded between 14:00 and 15:00 UTC, with RFQ requests timing out in the quote path and expiring at the gateway. The strongest evidence points to quote-service database connection pool exhaustion causing request latency and upstream timeouts, while the downstream FIX path appears healthy in the sampled data.

alternative_hypotheses.reason: Quote-service and rfq-gateway latency were elevated, but sampled CPU remained moderate at 42.2% to 47.0%, which does not support CPU saturation as the primary failure domain.
Pricing-service consumer lag was present but small in the sampled rows, and throughput stayed high. This does not support a backlog as the proximate cause of the observed quote timeouts.

Execution and FIX telemetry sampled at 14:01:48 and 14:02:24 remained connected, with zero reconnects and zero sequence gaps, so the FIX path does not explain the RFQ timeout symptoms in the returned evidence.

recommended_next_steps: Inspect quote-service DB pool configuration, pool waiters, and concurrent request counts around 14:00-14:03 UTC.
Check whether a recent same-service deployment or schema/query change preceded 14:00 UTC; no deployment evidence was returned here, so change attribution remains unproven.
Review the specific DB queries executed on the timed-out RFQs to identify slow or blocking statements.
Correlate application-thread saturation, connection acquisition timing, and database-side locks or saturation metrics if available.
Confirm whether timeouts resolved after the incident window and whether pool sizing or query optimization is warranted.
limitations: No runbooks or historical incidents were returned, so no validated remediation history is available in this assessment.
Returned samples cover only selected timestamps, not continuous telemetry; absence of evidence outside sampled rows is unknown, not disproven.
The evidence strongly supports pool exhaustion but does not independently establish why the pool became saturated.
A deployment/change record was referenced in the incident timeline, but no returned evidence ID for an actual deployment object was available, so change causality cannot be confirmed.

rca.executive_summary: RFQ processing degraded because quote-service database connections were fully exhausted, causing long DB waits, request latency spikes, and downstream RFQ timeouts/expirations. The sampled FIX path stayed healthy, making FIX instability unlikely in the returned evidence.
rca.impact: Two RFQs were observed to enter processing, then time out in quote-service and expire at rfq-gateway. rfq-gateway also logged upstream quote timeouts, indicating customer-facing RFQ availability degradation during the incident window.
timeline: 14:00:00 UTC: RFQ requested; quote-service log reports RFQ requests timing out after change.
14:00:36 UTC: Quote-service records DB wait and p95 latency breach.
14:01:24 UTC: Quote-service logs a processing timeout and a pool acquisition timeout with pool_size=40 and in_use=40.
14:01:36 UTC: DB pool utilization reaches 100% and the second RFQ also times out.
14:02:12 UTC: rfq-gateway logs upstream quote timeout after pool saturation.
14:02:00-14:02:24 UTC: RFQs expire at the gateway.
observed_evidence: Quote-service DB pool utilization reached 100%, indicating all connections were in use.
Quote-service DB wait and DB query latency were elevated at the sampled times.
Quote-service p95 request latency breached budget, rising from an 85 ms baseline to 1450 ms.
A log entry reported pool acquisition timeout with pool_size=40 and in_use=40.
rfq-gateway logged upstream quote timeout after pool saturation.
Business events show RFQs transitioning from requested/processing_started to processing_timeout and RFQ_EXPIRED.
FIX gateway and execution-service samples remained connected and stable in the returned rows.
Topology shows rfq-gateway depends on quote-service, and quote-service depends on pricing-service and risk-service.
rca.probable_root_cause: Quote-service database connection pool exhaustion caused queueing and DB wait inflation, which in turn drove request latency and RFQ processing timeouts.
contributing_factors: The returned samples show elevated request rate at the same time as saturated DB pool usage, which likely increased contention.
The investigation window contains only sampled telemetry, so the exact upstream trigger for saturation is not established.
The returned evidence does not show a failing FIX path, suggesting the issue was localized above execution/FIX handling.
immediate_next_steps: Validate the DB pool saturation mechanism in quote-service with thread, waiter, and acquire-time diagnostics.
Inspect blocking or slow DB queries associated with the affected RFQ trace IDs.
Confirm whether a recent configuration or deployment change altered pool sizing, request concurrency, or query patterns.
Monitor whether pool utilization, DB wait time, and request latency return to baseline after remediation.
follow_up_work: Add alerts on DB pool saturation and sustained acquire waits in quote-service.
Review query plans and connection usage patterns for the quote path.
Consider backpressure or admission control so rfq-gateway degrades more gracefully under quote-service contention.
Establish a change-correlation check for future incidents, since a change was mentioned but not evidenced here.

showcase.title: Database pool exhaustion
showcase.snapshot_label: Complete recorded evidence snapshot; independent of simulated animation progress. Cutoff is not continuous sample coverage.

identified: Pool saturation, long DB wait and processing timeouts align with RFQ expiry [METRIC-003-SERIES-QUOTE-SERVICE-DB_POOL_UTILIZATION-5, METRIC-003-SERIES-QUOTE-SERVICE-DB_WAIT_MS-5, LOG-003-002, BUSINESS-003-004, BUSINESS-003-005].
overstatements: The proposal asserts degradation through 15:00 UTC, although returned samples end at 14:02:24 UTC; the cutoff is not continuous time coverage.

Its confirmed-cause and 'caused' wording overstates causal evidence. The recorded timeout log reports pool_size=40 and in_use=40, but it does not prove the initiating saturation mechanism [LOG-003-002].

Pool utilization is 100% at 14:01:36, 87% at 14:01:48 and 100% at 14:02:24. Request rate falls from 256 to 240 between the last two samples, so a continuous rising-load story is unsupported [METRIC-003-POOL, METRIC-003-SERIES-QUOTE-SERVICE-DB_POOL_UTILIZATION-4, METRIC-003-SERIES-QUOTE-SERVICE-DB_POOL_UTILIZATION-5, METRIC-003-SERIES-QUOTE-SERVICE-REQUEST_RATE_PER_SECOND-4, METRIC-003-SERIES-QUOTE-SERVICE-REQUEST_RATE_PER_SECOND-5].

CPU/pricing/FIX exclusions apply only to the returned rows. The incident timeline mentions a deployment, but no deployment object was retrieved; higher request load does not independently prove the trigger.
unknowns: The initiating load/query/lock/connection-ownership mechanism, any preceding change, recovery and state after 14:02:24 UTC remain unknown. The events establish RFQ expiry, not financial loss.
validator_changes: The recorded gate accepted the failure domain and normalized 19 fields, including causal prose and observations. Its rewrites are rule-authored; they do not independently establish that each original field was erroneous.
The final advisory leaves the initiating cause unconfirmed and requires human review. Model and rule support scores are distinct and uncalibrated.
